Langwill 1980: 93 mentions one “descant trombone” in Burgdorf. Bachmann-Geiser 1998 mentions only a
“Diskant-Posaune” in Burgdorf, Inv. 1098. Leutenegger 1956 refers to instrument as a Diskantposaune Beat Gugger
(letter to the author of 25 May 1999) affirms there are two, both dated 1697.
signature: : “MACHT IOHANN CARL KODISCH NURNBERG 1697”; master’s mark, “I C K” with prancing horse.
pitch: B-natural with orig. mp; B-flat with modern mp. (according to Leutenegger 1956). My own observations: with slide closed, B-flat somewhat sharp
dimensions: h 1100, be 125. [from ****Guger letter?]. My meas.: bo1 9.9/10.0, bo2 10.2/10.2, mp rcvr 11.3 (new), slide exit 10.3 (new), be 123/124; slide sec. 1632.5, bell sec. 2638, overlap 21.3, total le 2616.7.
remarks:
Playing characteristics: “Spielbar,” ****according to typewritten catalogue, photocopy included in letter to the author from Beat Gugger, Museumsleiter, 25 May 1999). Slide works well; tone muffled. 
****Letter from Gugger: “Bestimmung: E. Leutenegger, Burgdorf. / Revidiert durch N. Spada, Burgdorf, am 3. März 1954.” (this is in a photocopied typescript included in letter). Repair at mp receiver and slide exit. Tubular slide stays; immoveable slide stay is recent replacement; moveable slide stay telescopic; immoveable slide stay has diagonal stripes and elaborate decoration—floral pattern in diagonal ribbons (shows considerable wear). Slide bow has wire ring, saddle with zigzag pattern; slide bow badly dented, has been repaired with solder; bow guard a later addition. Ferrules match instrument 1700. Bell bow has wire ring and saddle****zigzag?. Pin in hinge on bell stay, on bell-pipe side, 40.4mm long. Bell slightly beyond 4th pos. Examined by the author, June 1999.
